about: Independent verdict (0017) on the #254 correction (docs/decisions/0058) to the SRD conditions map: the crossReferences items added to three `scope: out`, `status: declined` entries whose evidence names a condition the same map defines. The reviewer was a separate agent context given only: the extracted text of pp. 180, 181, 182 and 189; a JSON before/after of the three changed entries; an id/citation/scope/status index of all 100 entries; the entries the new items resolve to, plus `condition-list`, which declares the vocabulary; and 0026, the decision record that governs the field. It was told not to read the repository, the issues, or any decision record numbered above 0026, so that nothing of the author's reasoning reached it. `sha256` is the final map. `rounds` keeps each round's verdicts unedited.
summary: Round 1: 1 agree, 2 disagree. Round 2 (final bytes): 3 agree, 0 disagree, both round-1 disagreements resolved and the round-1 completeness finding (e) withdrawn.
whatTheDisagreementsChanged: Round 1 disagreed with two of the three spans and the disagreement was upheld. The items were first written as the surrounding phrase -- `1 Exhaustion level` and `any Exhaustion levels` -- and the reviewer found that such a span no longer names the condition: it names a level count, which this map defines in a different entry, `exhaustion-levels`, at the same citation. A level-unit span paired with a condition-hub target is a precision defect even where the relation is right. It proposed the fix from the corpus's own words, suffocation's second sentence naming `Exhaustion` bare. Both were narrowed to the bare term, and `grappling-ends`' `A Grappled creature` was narrowed to `Grappled` with it, which round 2 called better rather than indifferent. Round 2 also established that the map follows one span rule and not two: quote the corpus's phrase `the X condition` where the evidence contains it, else the bare name -- so the pre-existing `the Incapacitated condition` item on the same entry was correctly left alone, and rewriting it would have been an over-correction.

openAfterTwoRounds.finding: `dead-revival-conditions` quotes `any conditions ... if the durations of those effects are still ongoing` and its own note names `condition-definition` in prose while declaring nothing. The shape 0026 section 1 exists to stop. `conditions` is not one of the fifteen names the vocabulary declares, so it is outside the question 0058 answers.

Dehydration (p. 181) is `suffocation-hazard`'s structural twin, carries the same `See also “Exhaustion.”` pointer, and has no entry at all, while two notes in this map count the routes into and out of Exhaustion without it. An entry-coverage question rather than a crossReferences one.

checkedBeforeMerge: Round 2 asked the author to confirm one entry it was never given, `heavily-obscured`. It declares `the Blinded condition` -> `blinded` and the `See also` sentence -> `blinded`, so the sweep is complete as round 2 concluded.
correctionToTheBrief: The round-2 brief said `diff.json`'s `before` side showed the round-1 bytes. It showed the pre-change original instead, which the reviewer noticed and recorded. That is the stronger baseline for the inertness claim -- it compares the final bytes against what was on `main` -- but it means the reviewer took the round-1 spans from its own round-1 verdict rather than verifying them again. Recorded because a reviewer's stated limit is part of the verdict.

verdicts.citation: p. 182, Grappling: “Ending a Grapple. A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the grapple’s escape DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.”
verdicts.reason: Anchoring: the string “A Grappled creature” occurs verbatim, capital A included, in this entry's own evidence. Target: “Grappled” is one of the fifteen names condition-list declares, and condition-list itself resolves the bare name “Grappled” to the entry `grappled`, whose evidence is the defining sentence “While you have the Grappled condition, you experience the following effects” (p. 182, Grappled [Condition]). resolvedBy is right. Pointer, not definition: grappling-ends cites “Rules Glossary / Grappling / p. 182”, a different glossary headword from “Grappled [Condition] / p. 182”; the two sit in different columns of the same page, so this is a naming outside the defining passage. Span: acceptable. “Grappled” is used attributively here and 0026 § 1 sanctions multi-word spans (“rolls Initiative”, “only the most protective degree of cover applies”), and every word of this span is the corpus's own naming of the condition — no quantifier is smuggled in. I would still mildly have preferred the bare “Grappled”, for consistency with condition-list's fifteen bare-name items; “the Grappled target” later in the same evidence is the same term and needs no second item. Note in passing that the sibling item on this entry, “the Incapacitated condition”, follows the corpus's own phrase, so the two items on one entry use two different span conventions.

verdicts.citation: p. 189, Suffocation [Hazard]: “When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each of its turns. When a creature can breathe again, it removes all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating.”
verdicts.reason: Anchoring passes: “1 Exhaustion level” is verbatim in the evidence. Pointer, not definition, passes: this entry cites “Rules Glossary / Suffocation [Hazard] / p. 189”, eight pages from “Exhaustion [Condition] / p. 181”. The relation is the right relation to declare. My objection is the span, and through it the target pairing. 0026 § 1 says `cites` quotes “the term as the evidence uses it”, and its examples (`surprised`, `Opportunity Attack`, `Difficult Terrain`) are terms, not terms plus a quantity. “1” is not part of any term. Worse, the span with the numeral and “level” attached no longer names the condition — it names a level count, and the entry that defines that unit is `exhaustion-levels` (p. 181: “Exhaustion Levels. This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain 1 Exhaustion level. You die if your Exhaustion level is 6.”), not the hub `exhaustion` (p. 181: “While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects.”). As declared, a level-unit span is paired with a condition-hub target; one of the two should move. The clean fix is at hand and costs nothing: the same evidence's second sentence names the condition in the corpus's own bare form — “all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating” — so `cites: "Exhaustion"` is available, is exactly the name condition-list declares and resolves to `exhaustion`, and would make this item both narrower and unambiguously correct. I would agree on that span. This is a precision defect, not a claim that the pointer is bogus; the hub does reach `exhaustion-levels` through its own dependsOn.

verdicts.citation: p. 180, Dead: “Unless otherwise stated, the creature returns to life with any conditions, magical contagions, or curses that were affecting it at death if the durations of those effects are still ongoing. If the creature died with any Exhaustion levels, it returns with 1 fewer level.”
verdicts.reason: Same defect as suffocation-hazard, and a shade worse. Anchoring passes: “any Exhaustion levels” is verbatim. Pointer, not definition, passes: “Rules Glossary / Dead / p. 180” is not “Exhaustion [Condition] / p. 181”. But “any” is a determiner, not part of the term, and the plural “Exhaustion levels” reads as the quantity the rule subtracts from — the unit stated by `exhaustion-levels` — while resolvedBy names the condition hub. Unlike suffocation, this evidence contains no second, bare naming of “Exhaustion”, so the correct narrowing here is `cites: "Exhaustion levels"` with `resolvedBy: exhaustion-levels`, or `cites: "Exhaustion"` (the substring is present inside “Exhaustion levels”) with `resolvedBy: exhaustion`. Either is defensible; the pair as declared is not. Note also the inconsistency this creates: three items across this map now quote the same term three different ways — “Exhaustion” (condition-list), “1 Exhaustion level” and “any Exhaustion levels” — all resolving to the same entry. 0026's § 4 claim rule is per-pointer and no declared SRD pointer phrase fires inside these spans, so nothing mechanical breaks; what breaks is the reviewability the term-anchored form was supposed to buy.

1.completeness: Within the three entries' quoted evidence I find one omission that I think should have been declared and none that should be withdrawn. (a) dead-revival-conditions quotes “the creature returns to life with any conditions, magical contagions, or curses that were affecting it at death if the durations of those effects are still ongoing” (p. 180). “conditions” here is the corpus's general term, whose meaning this map gives in `condition-definition` (Rules Glossary / Condition / p. 179), and the entry's own note already asserts the relation in prose — “the only passage that treats ‘the durations of those effects’ as a thing conditions have, which condition-definition says the corpus never fixes”. A relation stated in a note and not declared is exactly what 0026 § 1 exists to stop (#115's `surprise-glossary` was the same shape). It is not one of the fifteen names, so it is outside the literal wording of the question, but it is the one naming here that a reader would expect to be declared. (b) Second occurrences of an already-declared term need no second item and I do not ask for them: “all levels of Exhaustion” in suffocation-hazard and “the Grappled target” in grappling-ends are the same terms as the declared items. (c) No other name among the fifteen appears in these three evidences. “Incapacitated” in grappling-ends was already declared before this change. (d) Nothing declared should be withdrawn; all three items point at real terms with real defining entries. (e) Outside the three entries but visible on the four pages I was given, several other `scope: out` declined entries in entry-index.json sit on passages that plainly name one of the fifteen and, as far as this diff shows, gained nothing: `falling-hazard` (p. 182: “it has the Prone condition unless it avoids taking any damage from the fall”), `flying-fall` (p. 182: “you fall if you have the Incapacitated or Prone condition”), `heavily-obscured` (p. 182: “You have the Blinded condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space”), `grappling-imposes` (p. 182: “Successfully grappling a creature gives it the Grappled condition”), and, off these pages, `long-rest-exhaustion` (p. 185) and `malnutrition-hazard` (p. 185). I cannot see their evidence strings, so I cannot say whether they already carry items; if they do not, this change is a partial sweep of one class of pointer rather than a complete one, and 0026's own limit applies — “The table is not a census” — but a reviewer should be told which it is. Related observation: p. 181's Dehydration [Hazard] (“gains 1 Exhaustion level at the day's end. Exhaustion caused by dehydration can't be removed until the creature drinks the full amount of water required for a day”) is the exact structural twin of suffocation-hazard, and has no entry at all in entry-index.json while Suffocation and Malnutrition both do. That is an entry-coverage question, not a crossReferences one, but it is the kind of asymmetry the exhaustion notes lean on (“a third route into and out of Exhaustion”, “a fourth route out”) and the count of routes is stated without Dehydration being recorded.
1.limits: 1. I compared every field of all three entries before and after, byte for byte as given: id, name, locator.sourceId, locator.citation, kind, scope, clarity, dependsOn, evidence, status and note are identical in all three. Only `crossReferences` changed, and only by addition (grappling-ends kept its existing Incapacitated item, with the new item placed first, matching evidence order). No rule changes meaning. 2. I was given only four pages of a 364-page corpus, and only four entries in full (exhaustion, grappled, incapacitated, condition-list). I could not check the evidence strings of the other entries in entry-index.json, so finding (e) above is an inference from the corpus text plus citations, not a verified defect. 3. I could not check whether `check-map.py` actually accepts these items, whether the map's manifest declares pointer phrases that fire inside these evidences, or whether any counter in a README or the 0026 § 5 table needs updating for three more declarations. 4. 0026 § 1 is written in the direction in-scope entry names a `scope: out` entry. All three entries here are the reverse: `scope: out`, `status: declined` entries naming in-scope entries. I judged that legitimate, because the pre-existing Incapacitated item on grappling-ends already does it and § 4 contemplates a declined `scope: out` entry answering its own pointers. But § 1's text does not state the reverse direction, and if there is a later decision record that settles it, I was instructed not to look for it. 5. I did not read the repository, any issue or PR, or any author commentary, as instructed; no verdict above depends on anything but the five files.

verdicts.citation: p. 189, Suffocation [Hazard]: “When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of each of its turns. When a creature can breathe again, it removes all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating.”
verdicts.reason: This is exactly the span I proposed in round 1 and I confirm it. Anchoring: “Exhaustion” occurs verbatim and as a whole word twice in the entry's own evidence, and the second occurrence — “all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating” — is the corpus naming the condition in its bare form, standing alone, not inside a compound. Target: “Exhaustion” is one of the fifteen names condition-list declares, and condition-list itself resolves the bare string “Exhaustion” to `exhaustion`, whose evidence is the defining sentence “While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects” (p. 181). Span and target now agree: a condition name paired with the condition hub. The level-unit mismatch I objected to is gone, and `exhaustion-levels` is still reached from the hub by its own dependsOn. Pointer, not definition: the entry cites “Rules Glossary / Suffocation [Hazard] / p. 189”, eight pages from “Exhaustion [Condition] / p. 181”; this is a naming outside the defining passage. Span discipline: one term, no numeral, no determiner — the form 0026 § 1's own examples take. The narrowing claims no fewer pointers than before, because no SRD pointer phrase occurs anywhere in this evidence (there is no “see” construction in it), so § 4's claim rule is untouched.

verdicts.citation: p. 180, Dead: “If the creature died with any Exhaustion levels, it returns with 1 fewer level.”
verdicts.reason: This is the second of the two options I named as defensible in round 1, and I confirm it. Anchoring: “Exhaustion” occurs verbatim inside “any Exhaustion levels”, with a word boundary on both sides and the corpus's own capitalization — an attributive use of the condition name, the same grammatical shape as “A Grappled creature”, which I accepted in round 1. Target: bare “Exhaustion” is the string condition-list resolves to `exhaustion`; span and target now name the same thing. The determiner “any” and the plural “levels”, which were doing the damage, are out of the span. Pointer, not definition: “Rules Glossary / Dead / p. 180” is a different headword and page from “Exhaustion [Condition] / p. 181”. One residual, stated as a limit and not as a defect: the rule this entry records subtracts a level, and the unit it subtracts from is stated by `exhaustion-levels`; pointing at the hub is the coarser of the two defensible pairings, and the consequence is that no crossReferences item anywhere in the three files I was given points at `exhaustion-levels` — it is reachable only through `exhaustion`'s dependsOn. That is a reachability observation about the map, not a fault in this item, and it buys uniformity with suffocation-hazard and condition-list, which I judge the better trade. No SRD pointer phrase occurs in this evidence, so no claim is lost by narrowing.

verdicts.citation: p. 182, Grappling: “Ending a Grapple. A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the grapple's escape DC, ending the condition on itself on a success.”
verdicts.reason: Better, not merely indifferent, and I withdraw the “mildly” from my round-1 preference now that I can see the rest of the map. Anchoring: “Grappled” is verbatim and a whole word, twice (“A Grappled creature”, “the Grappled target”); it is not a substring of “Grappling”, so the headword does not create a spurious occurrence. Target: unchanged and correct, `grappled`, the hub at “Grappled [Condition] / p. 182”, a different glossary headword from this entry's “Grappling / p. 182”. Why better: the article and the head noun “creature” were the mapper's sentence, not the corpus's name for the term; stripping them leaves exactly the name condition-list declares, and it makes one item cover both occurrences without inviting a second item for “the Grappled target”. Ordering is right — the new item is placed first, matching evidence order, as the Incapacitated item's position relative to its own occurrence requires. No pointer phrase lies in this evidence (the “See also ‘Unarmed Strike’ and ‘Grappled.'” sentence belongs to `grappling-imposes`, not here), so narrowing claims nothing away.

2.siblingInconsistency: Correctly left alone, and my round-1 observation is answered rather than deferred. With `defining-entries.json` now showing the other declined entries, the map turns out to follow one rule, not two conventions: `cites` quotes the corpus's phrase “the X condition” where the evidence contains it — `falling-hazard` (“the Prone condition”), `flying-fall` (“the Incapacitated or Prone condition”), `grappling-imposes` (“the Grappled condition”), `long-rest-exhaustion` (“the Exhaustion condition”), and grappling-ends' own pre-existing “the Incapacitated condition” — and falls back to the bare name where the evidence has no such phrase. Checked against the corpus text: grappling-ends' evidence says “ending the condition on itself” and never “the Grappled condition”; suffocation-hazard's and dead-revival-conditions' evidences never say “the Exhaustion condition”. So all three corrected items take the fallback correctly, and the sibling takes the primary form correctly. The two items on grappling-ends look inconsistent and are not: they are one rule applied to two terms whose evidence differs. Rewriting the sibling to a bare “Incapacitated” would have been an over-correction — it would have broken the primary form shared with four other entries, and would have touched bytes outside this change's warrant. The author was right to leave it.
2.consistency: Resolved, on a stronger footing than the uniformity I asked for. Round 1 objected that the same term was quoted three ways across the map (“Exhaustion”, “1 Exhaustion level”, “any Exhaustion levels”), which defeats the reviewability the term-anchored form exists to buy. The two quantity-bearing spans are gone; every item that names the Exhaustion condition now reads “Exhaustion” (condition-list, suffocation-hazard, dead-revival-conditions) or the corpus's own “the Exhaustion condition” (long-rest-exhaustion), and Grappled likewise. A reviewer can now grep one string per term and find every naming of it. I consider the reviewability objection discharged.
2.findingE: withdrawn — all five entries I named and can now see (`falling-hazard`, `flying-fall`, `grappling-imposes`, `long-rest-exhaustion`, `malnutrition-hazard`) already carry crossReferences items naming the conditions their evidence uses, so this change is the completion of a sweep and not a partial one; the sole residual is `heavily-obscured` (Rules Glossary / Heavily Obscured / p. 182, “You have the Blinded condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space”), which is listed in entry-index.json but whose entry was not supplied in either round, so I still cannot confirm it declares “the Blinded condition” → `blinded` and the author should check that one entry before merging.
2.newDefects: None found. I looked for four kinds specifically. (1) Lost pointer claims: 0026 § 4 claims a pointer only when it lies wholly inside an occurrence of some `cites`, so a narrowed span can orphan a pointer; none of the three evidences contains any SRD pointer construction (no “see”, no “See also ‘…'”, no “earlier/later in”, no table reference), verified against pp. 180, 182 and 189 of corpus-pages.txt, so nothing was claimed before and nothing is claimed now. (2) Spurious occurrences created by shortening: “Grappled” does not occur inside “Grappling”, and “Exhaustion” occurs only as a whole word in both evidences. (3) Duplicate or overlapping items: none; the two items on grappling-ends have disjoint spans and distinct targets, and neither corrected entry has more than one item. (4) Over-correction: the author changed three `cites` strings and nothing else — did not touch the sibling Incapacitated item, did not retarget anything to `exhaustion-levels`, did not add speculative items. That restraint is correct.
2.completeness: Unchanged from round 1 except where superseded above. Finding (a) still stands and is the one thing this round does not address: dead-revival-conditions quotes “the creature returns to life with any conditions, magical contagions, or curses that were affecting it at death if the durations of those effects are still ongoing” (p. 180), the entry's own note asserts the relation to `condition-definition` in prose (“which condition-definition says the corpus never fixes”), and no item declares it. A relation stated in a note and not declared is the shape 0026 § 1 exists to stop. It is not one of the fifteen condition names, so it sits outside the literal wording of the question this change answers, and I do not make it a disagreement; I record that it remains undeclared after two rounds. Finding (b) (second occurrences need no second item) and (d) (nothing should be withdrawn) stand unchanged. Finding (c) stands: no further name among the fifteen appears in these three evidences. My round-1 aside about Dehydration [Hazard] (p. 181) also stands and is now sharper: its text “gains 1 Exhaustion level at the day's end. Exhaustion caused by dehydration can't be removed until the creature drinks the full amount of water required for a day. See also ‘Exhaustion.'” is the structural twin of both suffocation-hazard and malnutrition-hazard — it even carries the same “See also ‘Exhaustion.'” pointer that malnutrition-hazard declares an item for — and entry-index.json still has no entry for it at all, while Suffocation, Malnutrition and Long Rest all do. That is an entry-coverage question, not a crossReferences one, and it is outside this change's warrant; but the two exhaustion notes count the routes into and out of Exhaustion (“a third route”, “a fourth route”) and those counts are stated with a fifth route unrecorded. I would raise it as a separate issue rather than hold this change for it.
2.limits: 1. Field-by-field comparison of all three entries in diff.json: id, name, locator.sourceId, locator.citation, kind, scope, clarity, dependsOn, evidence, status and note are byte-identical before and after in all three. Only `crossReferences` differs, and only by addition; grappling-ends retains its pre-existing Incapacitated item unaltered. No rule changes meaning. 2. Note on the inputs, since it bears on what I can certify: the refreshed diff.json's `before` side is the pre-change original, not the round-1 state — grappling-ends' `before` carries only the Incapacitated item, and the other two carry no `crossReferences` at all. So the diff does not show me the round-1 bytes I reviewed; I take those from my own round-1 verdict, which quotes all three spans. This is sufficient to certify inertness against the original baseline, which is the stronger check, but I did not verify the intermediate state independently. 3. I still see only four pages of a 364-page corpus and twelve entries in full. `heavily-obscured` was named in my round-1 finding (e) and was not among the five supplied; it is the one entry on which finding (e) could still have force. 4. I could not run `check-map.py`, could not read the manifest to confirm which `pointerPhrases` the SRD corpus declares (my § 4 reasoning uses the seven patterns 0026 § 4 records, not the manifest itself), and could not check whether 0026 § 5's table or any README counter needs updating. 5. 0026 § 1 is written in the direction in-scope entry names a `scope: out` entry; all three of these are the reverse. I judged that legitimate in round 1 and still do — `defining-entries.json` now shows six declined `scope: out` entries doing it, so it is the map's settled practice and not an innovation here — but § 1's text does not state the reverse direction, and I was instructed not to look for a later record that might settle it. 6. I read only the six files named in my instructions; no verdict above depends on the repository, any issue, any PR, or any author commentary.
